Classic Sunday Roast with Rosemary and Garlic

Served at: First Sunday of Advent

Serves 4-6Prep 25 minCook 2 hours 30 min

Sunday Roast is a quintessential British meal, deeply rooted in tradition, often enjoyed after church on Sundays. For the First Sunday of Advent, it marks the beginning of the festive season, bringing families together for a comforting and hearty meal as they anticipate Christmas. This classic preparation features tender roasted beef, crispy potatoes, and sweet root vegetables, all bathed in rich gravy.

Ingredients

  • 3-4 pounds (1.4-1.8 kg) boneless beef chuck roast or top round roast
  • 2 pounds (900 g) Yukon Gold or Russet potatoes, peeled and quartered
  • 1 pound (450 g) carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch (5 cm) chunks
  • 1 large yellow onion, cut into thick wedges
  • 6 cloves garlic, peeled and smashed
  • 3 sprigs fresh rosemary
  • 3 tablespoons olive oil, divided
  • 1 teaspoon salt, plus more to taste
  • 1/2 teaspoon black pepper, plus more to taste
  • 2 tablespoons all-purpose flour (for gravy)
  • 2 cups (480 ml) beef broth (for gravy)
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) dry red wine (optional, for gravy)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 400°F (200°C).
  2. Pat the beef roast dry with paper towels. Season generously all over with 1 teaspoon salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.
  3. Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or roasting pan over medium-high heat. Sear the beef on all sides until deeply browned, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove the beef from the pan and set aside.
  4. In a large bowl, toss the quartered potatoes, carrot chunks, onion wedges, smashed garlic cloves, and rosemary sprigs with the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/4 teaspoon black pepper.
  5. Place the seared beef in the center of the Dutch oven or roasting pan. Arrange the seasoned vegetables around the beef.
  6. Roast for 1 hour at 400°F (200°C). Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (160°C) and continue to roast for another 1 hour to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until the internal temperature of the beef reaches your desired doneness (130-135°F / 54-57°C for medium-rare, 140-145°F / 60-63°C for medium). The vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
  7. Carefully remove the beef and vegetables from the roasting pan and transfer them to a large platter. Tent loosely with foil and let the roast rest for at least 15-20 minutes before slicing. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more tender and flavorful roast.
  8. While the beef rests, make the gravy. Place the roasting pan on the stovetop over medium heat. Skim off most of the excess fat, leaving about 2 tablespoons of drippings in the pan.
  9. Sprinkle the 2 tablespoons of flour into the drippings and whisk constantly for 1-2 minutes to create a roux.
  10. Gradually whisk in the beef broth and red wine (if using), scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer and cook, whisking occasionally, until the gravy thickens to your desired consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
  11. Slice the rested beef against the grain and serve immediately with the roasted vegetables and plenty of homemade gravy.

Tips

  • Use a meat thermometer for accurate doneness; remember the temperature will rise a few degrees as the meat rests.
  • Don't skip resting the meat; it's crucial for a juicy roast.
  • For extra crispy potatoes, par-boil them for 5-7 minutes before tossing with oil and roasting.
